narrative:
Your loan application was denied because the model estimated an 85% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. In practical terms, among applicants with a similar financial profile, about 85 in 100 would be expected to have serious repayment difficulty, so the bank treated the risk as too high.

The strongest factor was your checking account being overdrawn, below zero. This is much less common among approved applicants and pushed the decision strongly toward bad credit. The second most important factor was the size of the loan you requested: 10,297 DM, far above the approved average of about 3,020 DM. A larger loan means a larger repayment burden, so this also increased the risk. The third factor was the requested repayment period of 48 months, compared with an approved average of about 19 months. A longer term stretches your exposure and made the prediction less favorable. All three leading factors worked in the same direction, toward denial.

To improve your chances next time, focus on bringing your checking account into a positive balance, reducing the amount you borrow, and choosing a shorter repayment period if affordable. Building savings and waiting until your finances are stronger would also help. You can ask the bank what specific conditions would make a future application acceptable.
